decisions.choice: Hybrid confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-10-01 after four five-candidate rounds: full-width ink bands (near-black #1b1d21 on the light scheme, near-white #e7e9ee on the dark scheme, buttons inverted) for the hero on both pages, the home call to action and the join page's closing feedback-and-privacy band, each carrying the commit-eye rings as a 5% motif at the right edge (round-4 A plus E's mark, fainter); mono navigation and footer, 6 px square buttons, hairline slider cards with mono heads for the home features (round-2 A), a centred hairline check list for the facts (round-2 C), the phone right of the text in both heroes (round-3 B); the join page an 800 px centred column with centred steps and a mono checklist. Rejected along the way: tile grids for lists, a narrow one-column join page, graphite gradients, tonal and accent bands, a hairline-only hero.

decisions.question: How does repoglance.com go live?
decisions.rationale: The public pages need no CMS, Access or secret to serve (smoke on a fresh D1); exposing them on workers.dev first lets the maintainer see the real thing before DNS changes.
decisions.verification_ref: file:proof/hosting-20261001/PROOF.md#gate-2-custom-domains-2026-10-01 (public resolvers and --resolve: apex 200 from the seed, /_emdash 404; www 200; captures in swarm-pr-assets repoglance-site-live-20261001)

decisions.choice: Through Cloudflare Access only, in the order of docs/cms-access.md: the maintainer creates a self-hosted Access application for repoglance.com and www.repoglance.com on path _emdash with an Allow policy for their own email (one-time PIN), notes the Audience tag, sets CF_ACCESS_AUDIENCE, EMDASH_OPERATOR_ALLOWLIST (owner only) and EMDASH_ENCRYPTION_KEY as Worker secrets from their own terminal, and puts EMDASH_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN in the ignored .local/deploy.env; the agent builds with the team domain (which wires EmDash's access() and the guard), redeploys, proves anonymous and forged requests still get 404, and the maintainer completes EmDash setup through Access as the first (Admin) login, including the seed content so the pages switch to the CMS.
